question: In a recent review, the European Court of Auditors points the finger at the Commission, highlighting that around EUR 15 billion of the EUR 317 billion in cohesion funding disbursed in the 2014-2020 budget period were used in a non-compliant manner. The review claims that ‘the assurance framework for cohesion policy has not been effective in bringing it below the 2 % materiality threshold set out in the rules’1.

A February 2024 expert report on the future of cohesion policy2 welcomed by the Commission3 called for cohesion policy to be urgently reformed. The report claimed failings in the policy would primarily harm ‘migrants’, ‘ethnic minorities’ (page 6) and would fuel ‘anti-EU rhetoric’, to which ‘certain demographic groups that are often male, older and less educated’ are particularly susceptible (page 24). 1.
How does the Commission intend to address the shortcomings in how cohesion funding is used?
Does the Commission consider the ‘expert’ report’s clichéd description of those who vote for ‘Eurosceptic parties’ (page 22), tantamount to class contempt, to be justified?

Review 03-2024: ‘An overview of the assurance framework and the key factors contributing to errors in 2014-2020 cohesion spending’, https://www.eca.europa.eu/ECAPublications/RV-2024-03/RV-202403_EN.pdf Expert group’s recommendations for the future of EU cohesion policy, High-level Group on the Future of Cohesion Policy, 22.2.2024, https://www.europe-en-france.gouv.

fr/fr/ressources/rapport-detuderecommandations-du-groupe-dexperts-sur-lavenir-de-la-politique-de-cohesion. Report from experts on Cohesion Policy proposes ways to maximise the effectiveness and impact of Cohesion Policy in the future, 20.2.2024, European Commission press release.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (18.9.2024) The Commission provides reasonable assurance in its annual activity reports that for Cohesion policy, the level of error is lower than the materiality threshold of 2% for most programmes, and slightly above 2% for the overall expenditure, taking into account potential additional risks.

Where the level of error is material, the Commission performs multiannual controls and requests corrections to bring the error rate below 2% by the time of programme closure, based on the regulatory requirements for the application of financial corrections. Thus, the final error rate reported for all cohesion programmes is, according to the Commission’s calculations, approximately 1.3%.

In parallel, the Commission will continue all its administrative capacity building actions for programme authorities. It will also continue the use of its preventive and corrective tools and mechanisms in safeguarding the EU budget such as retention on interim payments, interruptions and suspensions of payments, and financial corrections.

The report1 mentioned by the Honourable Member was produced by a group of independent high-level specialists. Among other topics, the report describes some of the drivers of Euroscepticism, based on academic literature.
1 High-Level Group on the Future of Cohesion Policy, Forging a sustainable future together – Cohesion for a
